lead.event: OJK fines DSSA, BREN and CUAN, prompting a police investigation
lead.headline: OJK fines DSSA, BREN and CUAN Rp2.1 trillion as police plan probe
lead.blurb: Dian Swastatika Sentosa was fined Rp1.5 trillion, Barito Renewables Rp500 billion and Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Rp100 billion for suspected market violations. OJK tied the first fine to trading from 2023 to 2026 and the others to suspected IPO order-placement violations. National Police Chief Suyudi Ario Seto said Bareskrim Polri will deploy a team to investigate suspected crimes and take firm action once it gathers evidence.

market_structure_policy.event: MSCI consultation to reclassify Indonesia triggers a market selloff and institutional responses
market_structure_policy.headline: MSCI proposes standalone-market status for Indonesia as IHSG falls 14.91% in a week
market_structure_policy.blurb: MSCI’s consultation runs through April 2027, with a final decision due by 30 June 2027. Airlangga Hartarto said the deadline had been moved from November. OJK and the Indonesia Stock Exchange said they would continue reforms and communicate with MSCI, while Hans Kwee said verified governance improvements could reverse the proposal.

market_structure_policy.event: OJK fines parties over BREN and CUAN IPO share-allocation violations
market_structure_policy.headline: OJK fines parties Rp600 billion over BREN, CUAN IPO allocation violations
market_structure_policy.blurb: The penalties are Rp500 billion for parties tied to Barito Renewables’ offering and Rp100 billion for those tied to Petrindo’s. Neither issuer was fined directly. OJK found IPO shares had been pre-planned for a group affiliated with controlling shareholders and is reviewing offering documents while tracing fund flows.

earnings_guidance.event: RHB Sekuritas raises profit forecasts for TKIM
earnings_guidance.headline: RHB Sekuritas lifts TKIM profit forecasts by up to 24.8%
earnings_guidance.blurb: RHB Sekuritas raised Tjiwi Kimia’s estimates to US$368 million for 2026 and US$391 million for 2027, citing tax incentives and higher foreign-exchange gains. It expects the new 3-million-ton OKI facility to start commercial operations at end-2026 and reach 40% utilization in 2027, supporting earnings with pulp sales; its target implies 121% upside.
